content.title: About
content.content: Swiss reduced‑fat cheese (536) is a semi‑hard cheese with the characteristic holes, known for its mild nutty flavor. The lower fat content makes it lighter while preserving the traditional texture and aroma of classic Swiss cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Swiss cheese is made from cow’s milk in the Alps.
The holes are created by Propionibacterium bacteria that release carbon dioxide.
Fat reduction is achieved by partially skimming the milk and adding skimmed milk powder.
The cheese is often used in fondue, but the reduced‑fat version melts more quickly.
In the 2020s, demand for reduced‑fat Swiss cheese grew by more than 15 %.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides about 800 mg of calcium per 100 g, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Delivers 25 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Contains only 10 g of fat per 100 g, helping to control calorie intake.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Fermentation leaves live cultures that can benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains lactose, so people with intolerance should limit consumption.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to casein may experience reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salt is used during aging, so consider this if you follow a low‑sodium diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice thinly for sandwiches, add to salads, use in casseroles, or melt in fondue. It also works well grated over pasta and vegetable dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. For longer storage, the cheese can be frozen for up to 3 months, pre‑sliced into portions.
